title: Vendor onboarding — MSA/DPA & SLA review with BlueScale Health
summary: Procurement-led session to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs (uptime/latency credits), pricing approval process and vendor onboarding checklist. Redwood committed to share redlined MSA, SOC2 and DPA template, pricing spreadsheet and to coordinate legal and procurement timelines for PO issuance.

Priya to export perf benchmarks and expected latency SLOs for BlueScale workloads by 2025-02-20

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Legal Ops), Jenna Carter (BlueScale Procurement), Dr. Samir Patel (BlueScale CTO), Lena Ortiz (BlueScale Security), Marcus Lee (BlueScale Legal)

Auto-generated summary: Procurement & legal coordination on MSA/DPA/SLA/pricing. Some asides about dedicated capacity and data residency.

[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time for this. I'll kick us off — purpose today is to align on the MSA and DPA redlines, get clarity on the SLA expectations, and understand procurement timing so we can queue the onboarding.

[00:18] Jenna Carter: Great, thanks Alex. To be clear, procurement's on a fairly tight cadence — fiscal deadline Feb 28, so we need pricing approvals and PO by then if possible. Marcus from legal is here to handle contract details.

[00:30] Marcus Lee: Yep, yep, hi. We'll be running normal redline review. Primary asks: limitation of liability, data processing security language, and liability cap. Also need to see status of SOC2 and any subprocessors.

[00:44] Priya Shah: Absolutely — we'll share SOC2 report link and subprocessor list. On the technical side, BlueScale mentioned needing low p99 latency for inference in prod — do we have a target number?

[00:56] Dr. Samir Patel: We're targeting p99 under 250ms for our primary inference endpoint. If that's not feasible with hosted, we'll consider Dedicated or co-located options. Also data residency matters — PHI-ish data, so we need to ensure data never leaves our region.

[01:18] Alex Nguyen: Understood. From the contract side, Marco, Redwood's standard MSA has a 12-month SLA definition and credits structure — we can discuss adjustments. For DPA, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys on Private deployments; for hosted we have BYOK options with KMS integration.

[01:40] Marco Ruiz: Quick note — on indemnities we have a standard carve-out for customer data. We'll flag the clause. Marcus, any specific redline you want upfront?

[01:50] Marcus Lee: The limitation of liability cap — our procurement wants it uncapped for intentional misconduct and increased for data breach scenarios. Also need to ensure data deletion obligations are explicit in the DPA.

[02:05] Lena Ortiz: On security, we need encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS for any customer-provided PHI. Also audit logging and retention for 12 months at minimum. Are logs accessible via our SIEM?

[02:19] Priya Shah: Yes, we can push logs to customer SIEM via our log export; some configurations may be different for hosted vs private. For hosted, we can stream audit logs to a customer-owned GCS/S3 bucket; for Private we provide direct access to the control plane.

[02:38] Jenna Carter: Back on procurement — payment terms. We usually need 60-day net and PO numbers. Does Redwood accept 60 days? Also any early payment discounts?

[02:48] Alex Nguyen: Standard is 30 net; 60 net is possible but needs finance approval. I'll flag to our revenue ops. We don't typically offer early payment discounts on hosted usage, but for Dedicated/Reserved contracts we can discuss a 2% net-10 style term.

[03:05] Dr. Samir Patel: About deployment modes — if we go Dedicated, does Redwood still provide the same API semantics, and what is the SLA improvement?

[03:16] Priya Shah: API is consistent across modes. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and a higher SLA tier — e.g., 99.95% vs 99.9% on hosted; we can provide quantized latency profiles based on pool sizing. I'll send a short doc with expected token/sec and p99 numbers for your workloads.

[03:36] Marcus Lee: On the DPA, who is the subprocessor list and is there a model clause included for EU customers? BlueScale has EU patients so we might require EU SCCs.

[03:48] Marco Ruiz: We include a subprocessor list and we can add SCCs where required; the DPA template includes standard cross-border data transfer language. We'll mark SCCs as an add-on if needed.

[04:05] Jenna Carter: Quick question — do you require a security questionnaire? We generally send an RFP and security questionnaire to vendors.

[04:12] Alex Nguyen: Yes, BlueScale's security team can send the questionnaire; we also have an own vendor security pack with SOC2, penetration test summaries, and technical docs. We'll attach a short answers package for commonly asked questions.

[04:30] Lena Ortiz: We also want to confirm data retention and deletion timelines — backups included.

[04:36] Priya Shah: Standard retention is 30 days for logs, model KV is ephemeral unless explicitly cached; for customer data we have configurable retention and can provide deletion certificates on request. For backups, we store encrypted snapshots and can purge per DPA timelines.

[04:58] Dr. Samir Patel: Ok that's good. Another procurement question — are there any required entries in our supplier vetting system? Like insurance certificates, W9, or Dun & Bradstreet numbers?

[05:10] Jenna Carter: We'll need vendor risk questionnaire clearance, insurance, and W9. Also supplier set-up needs a registered tax ID and bank details for wire.

[05:22] Alex Nguyen: We can provide insurance certificate and W9. For bank wiring, Redwood's finance team will provide the paperwork after contract signature.

[05:32] Marcus Lee: Regarding SLA credits, we prefer a material remediation clause and explicit credit schedule. Are credits automatic or by claim?

[05:41] Marco Ruiz: Our policy is credits by claim with automatic monitoring evidence; we can discuss an automatic crediting mechanism for enterprise contracts.

[05:52] Priya Shah: If we detect infra anomalies we can also set automated fallback to a compatible lower-capacity model to preserve availability; that could help with uptime requirements.

[06:05] Lena Ortiz: About KMS — is BYOK available for the hosted product? We need both envelope encryption and key rotation control.

[06:12] Alex Nguyen: BYOK is supported; key rotation windows are customer-configurable within constraints. We'll include a technical note.

[06:22] Dr. Samir Patel: For pricing, how do you handle committed reserved capacity vs on-demand invoicing? I want a simple model to present to CFO.

[06:30] Alex Nguyen: Two paths — reserved (monthly commit) with discounted unit pricing and predictability, or pay-as-you-go hosted. For initial pilot we suggest a short committed Dedicated pool or a burstable reserved plan to mimic production. Pricing sheet will show per-token and per-embedding units plus reserved capacity breakouts.

[06:48] Jenna Carter: We'll need line-item pricing to attach to the PO. Also any cancellation terms? Procurement will look for termination for convenience with limited notice.

[06:58] Marco Ruiz: Termination for convenience is a negotiable clause; we usually propose 90 days' notice for reserved contracts and shorter for hosted. We'll surface a recommended approach but are open.

[07:14] Alex Nguyen: To keep things moving, the concrete asks from BlueScale: legal to send redline preferences, procurement to confirm PO date, security to send the vendor questionnaire. Redwood will send MSA/DPA redlines, SOC2 link, sample SLA language, and a pricing spreadsheet. Is that accurate?

[07:33] Jenna Carter: Yes. Can you also include a short onboarding runbook so our infra team knows steps and contact points?

[07:40] Priya Shah: We'll include a 1-page onboarding runbook that lists the contacts, expected artifact delivery, and sandbox access instructions.

[07:50] Marcus Lee: One more question on indemnity — do you carry cyber insurance and what's your coverage?

[07:56] Alex Nguyen: Yes, we carry a cyber policy; policy limits are in the vendor packet. We'll attach the certificate.

[08:05] Lena Ortiz: Anything else about audits? We might want a right-to-audit clause or periodic compliance attestation.

[08:12] Marco Ruiz: We generally provide SOC2 and quarterly attestations. Right-to-audit is usually handled via third-party attestations, we can discuss limited on-site audit language for enterprise deals.

[08:30] Alex Nguyen: Okay let's summarize next steps and owners — I'll do the redline and vendor packet, Priya handles technical benchmarks and runbook, Marco will prepare legal note on indemnity/SCCs, and BlueScale will circulate internal procurement timeline and questionnaire.

[08:46] Jenna Carter: We'll aim to have procurement approval by Feb 24 internally, then PO by Feb 28 if everything aligns.

[08:55] Dr. Samir Patel: If you can provide a short dedicated trial pool that would speed our performance validation — preferably a two-week window.

[09:04] Priya Shah: We can provision a short trial Dedicated pool — need to coordinate capacity. I'll follow up with estimates in the spreadsheet.

[09:12] Alex Nguyen: Great. Any blockers?

[09:15] Marcus Lee: None on our side aside from standard redline review.

[09:18] Lena Ortiz: None, we'll send the questionnaire today.

[09:21] Jenna Carter: Done. We'll look for the docs.

[09:24] Alex Nguyen: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after you've had a chance to review the redline and pricing — propose a follow-up legal call week of Feb 24.

[09:33] (Meeting ends)

References/attachments mentioned: MSA_redline_v1 (link to be shared), Redwood_SOC2_report.pdf (link), Pricing_breakout_blueScale.xlsx (link), Onboarding_runbook_v1.pdf (link)
